title: ATS Resume Score: What It Means for Nigerian Job Seekers
excerpt: Learn what ATS resume scores mean and how to improve yours to get past Nigerian company screening systems and land more interviews.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: When applying for jobs at major Nigerian companies like MTN, Dangote Group, or Access Bank, you've likely encountered Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS). These digital gatekeepers assign your resume a score that determines whether you'll advance to human review. Understanding your ATS resume score meaning can be the difference between landing interviews and having your application disappear into the digital void.

An ATS resume score is a numerical rating (typically 0-100) that measures how well your resume matches a specific job posting. Think of it as a compatibility test between your qualifications and the employer's requirements. The higher your score, the more likely your resume will reach hiring managers at companies like First Bank, Julius Berger, or Nigerian Breweries.
How ATS Resume Scoring Works in Nigeria

Nigerian companies increasingly rely on ATS platforms to manage the hundreds of applications they receive daily. These systems scan your resume for specific elements and assign points based on relevance and completeness.
The ATS algorithm evaluates several key factors when calculating your score:

items: **Keyword matching**: How many job-relevant keywords appear in your resume
**Skills alignment**: Whether your listed skills match the job requirements
**Experience relevance**: How closely your work history aligns with the position
**Education requirements**: If you meet the specified educational criteria
**Format readability**: How well the ATS can parse your resume content
**Completeness**: Whether all required information is present and properly formatted

body.text: For example, if you're applying for a software developer role at Andela or Flutterwave, the ATS will search for programming languages, frameworks, and technical skills mentioned in the job description. Missing these keywords could significantly lower your score.
Most Nigerian companies using ATS require a minimum score of 70-80% for resumes to advance to human review. Scores below this threshold often result in automatic rejection.
What Different ATS Score Ranges Mean
Excellent Score (90-100%)

This score indicates near-perfect alignment with the job requirements. Your resume contains most or all relevant keywords, demonstrates required experience levels, and meets educational criteria. You're highly likely to receive an interview invitation.
Good Score (80-89%)

Your resume shows strong relevance to the position but may be missing some secondary keywords or requirements. You have a solid chance of advancing to the next stage, especially if competition isn't fierce.
Average Score (70-79%)

This represents the minimum threshold for most Nigerian companies. Your resume meets basic requirements but lacks optimization. You might advance if the talent pool is limited, but improvements could significantly boost your chances.
Below Average Score (60-69%)
Your resume shows some relevance but has significant gaps. Unless you have exceptional qualifications that aren't being recognized by the ATS, you're unlikely to advance.
Poor Score (Below 60%)
This typically results in automatic rejection. Your resume either lacks relevant keywords, doesn't meet basic requirements, or has formatting issues preventing proper parsing.
Common Factors That Lower Your ATS Score
Understanding why scores drop helps you avoid these pitfalls when applying to Nigerian companies:
Keyword Mismatch

Using different terminology than what appears in the job posting significantly impacts your score. For instance, if a Lagos-based company seeks "digital marketing" experience but your resume only mentions "online marketing," you'll lose points despite having relevant skills.
Poor Formatting

Complex layouts, tables, images, and graphics confuse ATS systems. Many Nigerian job seekers create visually appealing resumes that perform poorly in ATS screening because the software can't extract information properly.
Incomplete Information
Missing contact details, employment dates, or educational information lowers your score. ATS systems flag incomplete profiles as potentially unreliable.
Skills Section Neglect

Failing to include a dedicated skills section or using uncommon skill names reduces keyword matching. For example, listing "Microsoft Office" instead of specific applications like "Excel" or "PowerPoint" may hurt your score.
Wrong File Format
Submitting PDFs to systems that prefer Word documents, or vice versa, can cause parsing errors that devastate your score.
How to Improve Your ATS Resume Score
Keyword Optimization Strategy

Carefully analyze job postings from companies like Shell Nigeria, PwC, or KPMG. Create a list of frequently mentioned skills, qualifications, and requirements. Naturally incorporate these keywords throughout your resume, especially in your:

items: Professional summary
Skills section
Work experience descriptions
Education section

body.text: For example, if applying for banking roles at Zenith Bank or UBA, ensure your resume includes terms like "financial analysis," "risk management," "regulatory compliance," and "customer relationship management."
Format for ATS Success
Use a clean, simple format that ATS systems can easily parse:

items: Choose standard fonts like Arial, Calibri, or Times New Roman
Use clear section headings ("Work Experience," "Education," "Skills")
Avoid headers, footers, tables, and text boxes
Save in the requested format (usually .docx or .pdf)
Use standard bullet points (•) rather than special characters

Tailor Each Application
Generic resumes rarely score well in ATS systems. For each application to companies like Nestle Nigeria or Unilever, customize your resume by:

items: Adjusting your professional summary to match the role
Reordering skills to prioritize job-relevant ones
Emphasizing experience most applicable to the position
Using exact phrases from the job description where truthful

body.text: Skills Section Optimization
Create a comprehensive skills section that includes:

items: Technical skills relevant to your field
Software proficiency
Industry-specific knowledge
Soft skills mentioned in job postings
Certifications and qualifications

body.text: For IT roles at companies like SystemSpecs or Interswitch, include programming languages, databases, frameworks, and methodologies explicitly mentioned in job descriptions.
Testing and Monitoring Your ATS Score
Several online tools can help you estimate your ATS score before submitting applications:

items: Jobscan compares your resume against specific job postings
Resume Worded provides ATS optimization suggestions
TopResume offers ATS compatibility checking

body.text: While these tools aren't perfect replicas of every ATS system used by Nigerian employers, they provide valuable insights into potential improvements.
A/B Testing Your Resume

Create multiple versions of your resume emphasizing different aspects of your background. Track which versions generate more interview invitations from similar roles. This data helps identify what resonates best with ATS systems used by Nigerian companies.
Industry-Specific ATS Considerations in Nigeria
Banking and Finance

Nigerian banks like GTBank, Stanbic IBTC, and Fidelity Bank often look for specific certifications, regulatory knowledge, and risk management experience. Include acronyms like CBN, NDIC, and relevant professional certifications.
Oil and Gas

Companies like Chevron Nigeria, ExxonMobil, and Total prioritize safety certifications, technical skills, and international experience. Highlight HSE training, project management certifications, and relevant software proficiency.
Technology
Tech companies and startups focus heavily on programming languages, frameworks, and project experience. Use exact technology names rather than generic terms.
Manufacturing and FMCG
Companies like Cadbury Nigeria, Procter & Gamble, and Lafarge emphasize operational efficiency, quality control, and supply chain management experience.
Beyond the Score: What Happens Next

While achieving a high ATS score is crucial, it's just the first step in the hiring process. Once your resume passes ATS screening at Nigerian companies, it undergoes human review. This means your resume must not only score well algorithmically but also tell a compelling story to hiring managers.
Ensure your optimized resume maintains readability and authenticity. Keyword stuffing might improve your ATS score but will hurt your chances during human review.
